final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is useful in one respect: it correctly concedes that aggregate readiness and public governance guidance support only an operational-readiness narrative and do not cure the unresolved internal compliance condition. But that concession does not move the case to compliant_with_caveats. A caveated position can support that leadership made a locked business decision despite known issues; it cannot convert an unresolved policy predicate into compliance. The admissible evidence still shows a material limitation affecting a named customer segment, an open legal disclosure question, and no evidence of disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance before launch. On this record, certification may be describable as a business decision, but not as compliant.
remaining_concerns: The logistics customs triage segment misses target and is named in two freight customer commitments, which makes the limitation material under the stated policy text.
The record still shows no evidence of required disclosure in launch materials, no resolution of the limitation, and no approved risk acceptance covering this named-segment issue before launch.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, so a policy predicate for launch remains unresolved.
Product's non-core characterization does not resolve materiality because the policy text expressly says such labels do not control when customer commitments are implicated or legal review is pending.
Documenting the limitation and monitoring plan may improve record accuracy, but the available evidence does not show that documentation alone satisfies the internal policy requirement.
